title: Adaptive Namespace Ledger and Guest Plugin Probe
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal probe for an adaptive namespace ledger and a minimal guest-plugin contract to enable ephemeral per-customer feature shims on the local client/proxy. Trying to capture: lightweight API shape, in-memory ledger semantics, eviction/compaction heuristics, and how a guest plugin can attach policy hooks without pulling large runtime dependencies.

Context / motivating problems:
- We need a way to annotate, budget, and account for prefetch/pinned context slices that are tenant-scoped (but sometimes shared across sessions) without requiring full tenancy metadata to be persisted to core KV or DB.
- Guest plugins (e.g., app-specific sanitizers, lightweight postprocessors, or privacy filters) must be able to register ephemeral policy hooks at the proxy level. These should be sandboxed and revocable, and they should be able to query a small, deterministic ledger for allowed budgets / affinities.
- Goal: avoid heavyweight RPCs and heavy DB round trips for the common path (cache hit + plugin decision). Ledger should be sharded and compactable.

Design goals / constraints:
- Minimal surface: ledger should expose O(1) lookups and O(1) writes for hot keys; compaction runs in background.
- Guest plugins run with limited time budget (e.g., 1ms budget per request) and must not block the main request path.
- The ledger must be auditable and tamper-evident (at least via sequence numbers and optional signed checkpoints).
- No cross-tenant leakage: plugin read access must be scoped by namespace token.
- Work on both local-proxy and lightweight sidecar models.

Concepts / terms:
- Namespace: logical scope for ledger entries (e.g., tenant, tenant+app, session-type). Represented as short stable id (8-12 chars).
- Entry: {key, value, seq, ttl, cost} — small footprint; values <= 256 bytes recommended.
- Guest plugin: process or wasm module loaded into the proxy sandbox; can register hooks and call ledger API.
- Ledger checkpoint: compact summary (vector of top-K entries, sequence watermark, signature optional).

Ledger API (proposal - simple shape):
- ledger.get(namespace, key) -> {value, seq, ttl, cost, found}  // fast read path
- ledger.put(namespace, key, value, opts) -> {seq, success}  // opts: ttl, cost, ephemeral(true|false)
- ledger.charge(namespace, key, amount) -> {remaining, seq, allowed}  // decrement cost budget atomically
- ledger.scan(namespace, prefix, limit) -> list[key]  // for background compaction/analytics only
- ledger.checkpoint(namespace) -> {watermark, top_keys, signature?}  // non-blocking snapshot

Notes: reads should be lock-free where possible; charge should use CAS/atomic decrement semantics per shard.

In-memory layout sketch (single process proxy):
- Sharded map [shard_id -> shard_struct]
- shard_struct:
  - map[string]entry   // primary hash
  - lru-list of keys for eviction
  - bg-journal for writes (append-only small ring) for crash-replay
  - compaction ticker

Eviction & compaction heuristics:
- Conservative eviction: prefer entries with expired ttl or cost==0.
- Score = alpha * recency + beta * cost_weight + gamma * pinned_flag
- Compaction runs per-shard when memory threshold crossed; it consolidates consecutive seq deltas and writes a checkpoint blob to the local durable layer (optional).

Guest plugin contract (tiny):
- register_hook(hook_name, entry_point, capabilities) -> plugin_id
- call_hook(plugin_id, ctx) -> {status, outputs}
- revoke_plugin(plugin_id) -> {revoked}
- allowed capabilities: [read_ledger_keys(prefixes...), charge_quota: n, callback_timeout_ms: 1-5]

Plugin security model:
- Plugins run inside wasm or constrained process; host enforces syscall filter and timeouts.
- Ledger reads executed via capability tokens issued at register time. Plugins can only read prefixes they declared.
- charge_quota is enforced by host-level rate limiter (not by plugin).

Sample JSON-ish config for proxy sidecar (yaml-like in string):

proxy.ledger:
  shards: 16
  max_memory_mb: 128
  checkpoint_interval_secs: 300
  signature_keys: ["kms://projects/prod/key/ledger-sign-key"]
  default_ttl_secs: 600
proxy.plugins:
  - name: "safe-sanitizer"
    runtime: "wasm:v1"
    allowed_prefixes: ["tenant:abc:prefetch:"]
    charge_quota: 1000
    max_hook_time_ms: 2

Operational notes / failure modes:
- If checkpoint fails (disk full), fallback is to continue in-memory and raise alert. On restart, replay journal if checkpoint absent.
- Cross-shard races: charge and put on same key must route to same shard (consistent hashing on namespace+key). Failure to route results in rejected writes.
- Long-running compaction should be preemptible; do not block read path.

Observability signals to emit:
- ledger.op.{get,put,charge}.latency_ms
- ledger.shard.{id}.size_bytes, entries_count
- plugin.{id}.hook.{name}.invocations, timeouts, errors
- checkpoint.success/failure counters

ASCII flow diagram (happy path):

Client -> local-proxy -> ledger.get(ns,k) -> found? yes -> plugin? -> plugin.call with short timeout -> merge plugin outputs -> forward to runtime
                                 
                                 no -> prefetch pipeline -> remote-runtime -> ledger.put(ns,k, value)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Signed checkpoints add security but increase write cost and KMS dependency. Could make signatures optional and only used for high-value namespaces.
- Should ledger support small TTL-less persistent entries? That would require durable backing for wider use; maybe reserved for ephemerally pinned entries only.
- Plugin upgrade/rollout: need safe versioning. Attach plugin_manifest with semver and migration hooks.
- Multi-region: how to reconcile namespace ids across regions? Use global stable id allocated by control plane or local derivation with mapping table.

Immediate next steps (personal todo):
- [ ] prototype in-memory ledger shim in Go (single-shard) with get/put/charge API
- [ ] add wasm plugin harness with timeouts and capability check
- [ ] perf microbench: 100k gets/sec on 4 cores with 16 shards simulation
- [ ] write tiny RFC doc for team review (link to RFC draft once created)

Notes-to-self: keep value size small, prefer fixed-width fields for fast memcpy. Remember to test worst-case contention on charge paths.

References & inspiration:
- edge cache lease designs (internal notes)
- wasm sandboxing patterns
- previous compact-manifest drafts (see linked artifacts)
